summary:
On Aethel 12, 1040, at approximately 8:18 PM, Wario and Waluigi accepted an interview invitation from an unidentified host who promised a massive pile of gold at the conclusion of their conversation. Upon arriving at what appeared to be a standard interview office, Wario immediately demanded to skip all polite preliminaries and proceed directly to discussions of treasure, while Waluigi adopted a posture of cynical suspicion, brandishing a wilted red rose as both a prop and a potential weapon. The Host summoned two goons who entered carrying heavy bags of money, which immediately captured the full attention of both brothers. However, when the Host produced a floating book containing Waluigi's private debt ledgers—detailing his catastrophic financial obligations to Wario, including compound interest rates that would make a usurer uncomfortable and unitemized 'Wario Brand Services Rendered'—and Wario began gloating about these debts, the Host snapped his fingers and caused both the bags of gold and the floating book to vanish. The Host announced that the treasure would only be restored if Wario and Waluigi cooperated fully with the interview process.

When the brothers proved reluctant to cooperate, the Host escalated dramatically. He began snapping his fingers to break the lights in the room one by one, plunging the space into progressive darkness. The room then went completely pitch black, and when a single light flickered back on, the interview table had been replaced by a grand piano. The Host began playing the piano and singing cryptic lyrics about news, degrees, and who interviews whom. A crown flew through the air and landed on the Host's head, revealing a Star Shard embedded within it that began to shine with divine power. The Host then revealed his true identity as the Toad God, a divine entity whose 'divinity is past infinity.' He pointed at Wario and Waluigi and dragged them toward him through the air using telekinetic force generated by the Star Shard.

What followed was an extended sequence of reality-warping torment designed to demonstrate the Toad God's absolute power and break the will of his interview subjects. The Toad God disabled gravity for Wario and Waluigi, causing them to fall flat like pancakes. He then danced, rolled around, and pointed at Waluigi, stating 'dont need to scream if you ain't go a mouth' before magically removing Waluigi's mouth entirely, leaving smooth, unbroken skin where his lips, teeth, and jaw had been. Waluigi was rendered completely silent, able only to produce muffled, terrified sounds as he clawed at his face in panic.

The Toad God then summoned a deck of cards depicting Wario, Waluigi, Markop, and Remi, and slammed them down on the flattened brothers with a giant cosmic hand. He flicked the cards, sending Wario and Waluigi flying through the air while singing about the 'doughnut world' being the only place they would ever be. He stopped them before they hit the floor, flicked them upward into a trapdoor in the ceiling where a giant fist punched them downward into a winding staircase dimension. They tumbled down the stairs as the Toad God continued singing about not forgetting who was running the interview. They fell into a giant microphone, which the Toad God tapped and made disappear.

The office snapped back into existence. The Toad God handed Wario a bomb that exploded in a cartoon-style explosion, leaving Wario completely blackened with soot, his hair standing in scorched spikes, smoke rising from his mouth. A Chain Chomp appeared and chewed up what appeared to be Waluigi—but it was revealed to be a plush version of Waluigi that burst with stuffing rather than blood. The Toad God stated simply: 'I am the host I run the place you don't need to know my name.'

Waluigi was then placed in an electric chair. The Toad God said 'oh what a shock' and electrocuted him. Wario, stumbling around in the disoriented aftermath, walked directly into a cardboard cutout of Waluigi, hitting his head. The Toad God began tap-dancing while singing about running the place.

In what may have been the most humiliating moment of the encounter, the Toad God picked Wario up by the neck, dragged him close, and smudged him into the ground like a piece of discarded chewing gum. Wario lay there, flattened and stained, demanding his dignity back while mostly just looking like a greasy streak on the floor that was 'already setting.'

The Toad God then snapped his fingers again. Waluigi's mouth was restored. The room shifted to a dance stage where both Wario and Waluigi found themselves wearing sharp tuxedos, performing a coordinated jazz routine with backup dancers that were doppelgängers of themselves. The Toad God, now in a black suit and tie, sang about a 'public relations cleanse.' The stage then shifted again, with the Toad God walking down a giant staircase attached to a massive cake—Peach's Cake, the very recipe Wario had long claimed to possess.

Then, Wario and Waluigi disappeared entirely. Waluigi was teleported through a sequence of visions while the Toad God's voice echoed in his head. First, he appeared on a train where he saw Luigi and E. Gadd, accompanied by the phrase 'So play the games.' Second, he appeared in Peach's Royal Chambers where Peach was frozen in time, dead, accompanied by 'and just ignore the pains.' Third, he appeared in the Regal Empire Diet where people were voting and a giant screen displayed 'MUSHROOM KINGDOM CONTAINMENT ACT - PASSED,' accompanied by 'cause all that remains is how you prime your brains.' During this sequence, something was attached to Waluigi's head and his brain was 'primed.'

Wario experienced a similar but distinct sequence, being juggled like a ball by the Toad God, tied to train tracks, forced to run into walls, made to fall off cliff edges, and finally exploded in a massive cartoon explosion as the Toad God took a bow and the music ended.

The office reappeared one final time. Wario and Waluigi were back in their chairs, the single light on, everything appearing normal though both were deeply traumatized. The Toad God asked if they understood the power of a single Star Shard, explaining that he had once possessed all of them at once but the power was too great—it started cracking, so he had to split them. When Waluigi asked if this was why everything felt broken, the Toad God denied responsibility for the brokenness but claimed he would have a hand in fixing it.

When pressed about his plans, the Toad God dismissed them, stating 'why would I tell you my plans, you will be mere pawns in it anyway.' He then revealed the true nature of his cosmic perspective: the world is a doughnut, and a 'Big Bite' has already been taken out of it by a Cosmic Jester. He referenced how Estalia responded by sending troops to the other side of the doughnut. The Toad God agreed with the Jester's premise: 'He had a point, we should take more bites and get to the jelly filling.'

The Toad God called out Waluigi for not documenting the Big Bite in Walupedia. Waluigi attempted to deflect, claiming the events were unconfirmed rumors. The Toad God shut this down immediately, stating there is a literal bite-sized hole in the planet that caused depopulation, it was all over the news, and the Cosmic Jesters are scattered because of it. Waluigi was lying because he was too scared to document it.

Wario, ever the opportunist, interrupted the existential dread to negotiate his cut of the operation. He offered his services as 'Chief Acquisitions Officer' or 'Head of Crisis Merchandising,' promising infrastructure, muscle, and grit. He warned the Toad God not to treat him like disposable scrap metal again, threatening lawsuits and supply chain collapses.

The Toad God, seemingly amused by Wario's relentless capitalism, agreed they should talk in private—without Waluigi. He pointed at Waluigi, called him uncooperative, and asked if he had any last words before being sent back.

Waluigi, betrayed and indignant, stood up and protested being called uncooperative when he was merely being rational. He glared at Wario, who was already calculating the value of a private deal. Waluigi delivered his parting warning: 'Go on! Negotiate! Make your little deals! But remember… even a pawn can trip the player if they move just the right way at the right time! Waaaaah!' He pulled his cap low over his eyes to hide tears and backed away into the gloom.

This article documents the full sequence of events, the cosmic revelations, the anatomical violations, the psychological torment, and the ongoing implications for the Doughnut World, the Star Shards, the Cosmic Jesters, and the relationship between Wario and Waluigi as one brother negotiates with a god while the other is cast aside. Waluigi notes for the historical record that he was mouthless for a significant portion of this encounter, his dignity has not recovered, and he intends to document the Big Bite in Walupedia immediately upon regaining access to his archives, consequences be damned. WAH.
description:
## Author's Note on Trauma, Anatomical Alteration, and Archival Responsibility

Waluigi must begin this entry by formally acknowledging that the events documented herein were experienced under conditions of extreme duress, temporary anatomical alteration (specifically, the complete magical removal of his mouth), sustained psychological torment, and at least three distinct instances of being flattened, smudged, or otherwise treated as a two-dimensional object rather than a sentient being. Waluigi's recall of the sequence is unusually sharp and detailed, not because of any enhanced memory capacity, but because trauma functions as an excellent preservative for experience. The mind does not forget what it cannot process, and Waluigi has not yet processed being turned into gum.

Waluigi's objectivity regarding the Toad God is fundamentally compromised by several factors: (1) the Toad God removed Waluigi's mouth, which is Waluigi's primary instrument of expression, intimidation, and identity; (2) the Toad God subjected Waluigi to an electric chair; (3) the Toad God dismissed Waluigi as 'uncooperative' and excluded him from negotiations that may determine the fate of existence itself; (4) the Toad God revealed that Waluigi's financial desperation (specifically, the threat of kidney donation to settle debts) was known and could be exploited; and (5) the Toad God demonstrated power that renders Waluigi's entire sense of agency meaningless.

Waluigi acknowledges these compromises and includes them here so that the reader may calibrate their interpretation of this account accordingly.

The reader should approach this entry with the understanding that the Toad God is not a metaphor, not an allegory, not a symbolic representation of corporate power or existential dread (though he may incidentally represent those things). He is an actual divine entity, wearing a suit and tie, wielding a Star Shard of genuine cosmic power, and conducting reality itself like a hostile jazz routine. The interview was not an interview in any conventional sense. It was a demonstration of absolute power framed as a conversation, designed to remind two greedy, desperate men that they are small, edible, entirely disposable, and that their entire existence occurs within a context they do not control and barely comprehend.

Waluigi has chosen to document this encounter in full detail not because he enjoys reliving it (he does not; the memory of mouthlessness causes him to instinctively touch his face even now), but because the historical record requires it. The Toad God's revelations about the Doughnut World, the Big Bite, the Cosmic Jesters, the Star Shards, and the Mushroom Kingdom Containment Act are of such significance that they cannot be left to rumor, speculation, or Wario's self-interested retelling. Wario will tell this story as a negotiation. Waluigi tells it as a witness to cosmic horror.

Additionally, Waluigi must address his failure to document the Big Bite in Walupedia prior to this encounter. The Toad God was correct: Waluigi omitted the Big Bite from his archives out of fear. Documenting a literal hole in the world caused by a cosmic entity implies a scale of vulnerability that Waluigi, who has built his identity on being the underestimated underdog who triumphs through cunning, prefers not to confront. To acknowledge the Big Bite is to acknowledge that there are forces in the universe that cannot be outsmarted, only survived or consumed. Waluigi was not ready to write that article.

He is still not ready.

But he will write it now, because the Toad God has made it clear that ignorance is not a shield, and Waluigi would rather be a documented victim of cosmic forces than an undocumented one.

This entry is longer than usual. It is more detailed than usual. It includes more philosophical reflection than usual. This is because the events themselves were longer, more detailed, and more philosophically significant than anything Waluigi has previously documented. Waluigi asks for the reader's patience. Waluigi also asks for the reader's understanding that when he writes 'WAH' at the end of sections, it is not merely a signature but an expression of existential frustration that language cannot fully contain.

WAH.

## Section I:


The Invitation and the Bait

The invitation arrived through channels Waluigi has not fully traced. It was not delivered by mail, by messenger, by magical transmission, or by any conventional means. It simply appeared in Waluigi's awareness, a knowledge that there was an interview, that gold would be provided, that Wario would be there, and that attendance was expected. Waluigi suspects the Toad God simply willed the invitation into their minds, which is consistent with the level of power demonstrated later.

Wario's reaction to the invitation was immediate and predictable. He saw 'gold' and 'interview' and calculated that the gold would outweigh the inconvenience of the interview. Wario does not attend interviews for the sake of publicity or legacy-building. Wario attends interviews when he believes he can extract tangible value from them. In this case, the promised 'massive pile of gold' was sufficient incentive. Wario did not question who was conducting the interview, where it would be held, what the terms were, or whether the gold was real. He simply showed up, because Wario shows up anywhere gold is mentioned, even if the venue is a dimly lit room with an increasingly hostile interviewer and a distinct smell of cosmic dread.

Waluigi showed up for more complex reasons. First, Wario showed up, and Waluigi does not have the luxury of ignoring opportunities that Wario pursues. The Wario Bros arrangement, such as it is, requires Waluigi to be present when Wario is making decisions that could affect their shared financial situation. Second, Waluigi is, despite his protests to the contrary, curious. The promise of an interview with someone who could produce a 'massive pile of gold' suggested either enormous wealth or enormous power, and Waluigi has learned to pay attention to both. Third, and this is the reason Waluigi is least comfortable acknowledging, Waluigi hoped that the interview might provide a resolution to his debt situation.

If the Host was powerful enough to produce gold from nothing, perhaps he was powerful enough to restructure or eliminate Waluigi's obligations to Wario.

This hope was naive.

Waluigi knows this now.

He did not know it then.

The location of the interview was an office that appeared standard in every respect. There was a table. There were chairs. There was a single light source that flickered occasionally. There were shadows in the corners that seemed deeper than they should be. There was an interviewer who sat across from them, whose face Waluigi now remembers as unremarkable, which in retrospect was the first sign that this was no ordinary interviewer. Ordinary interviewers have remarkable faces. They have expressions, tics, tells. This interviewer had none of these. He was a blank space that happened to be wearing a suit.

The interview began at 8:18 PM on Aethel 12, 1040. The Host welcomed them. Wario immediately interrupted to demand gold. Waluigi adopted a posture of cynical suspicion, crossing his spindly arms and brandishing a wilted red rose that he had pulled from his vest. This rose was not a romantic gesture. It was a prop, a symbol of Waluigi's theatricality, and potentially a weapon if the situation required it. Waluigi has used roses as distractions, as tools for picking locks, and once, memorably, as a means of delivering a mild toxin to a particularly annoying rival. The rose was wilted because Waluigi had been carrying it for some time, and because Waluigi's life, like his roses, tends toward the faded and the desperate.

Wario's opening statement was characteristic: 'Wahahaha! An interview? Listen here, kid, time is money! And my time is incredibly expensive! I didn't show up here to talk about my childhood or my feelings—I'm here because you promised there'd be a massive pile of gold at the end of this little chat!'

This statement reveals several important aspects of Wario's psychology: (1) Wario views time exclusively through the lens of monetary value; (2) Wario has no interest in emotional vulnerability or personal history; (3) Wario believes that promises of gold are binding contracts that must be fulfilled immediately; and (4) Wario's laugh, 'Wahahaha,' functions as both a greeting and a threat. Waluigi has heard this laugh thousands of times. He knows its variations. The laugh in this instance was the 'I am about to demand something and will not accept no as an answer' variation.

The Host did not respond to Wario's demands with anger or frustration. He simply snapped his fingers. Two goons entered, carrying heavy bags that clinked with the sound of coins. Wario's eyes widened. Waluigi felt his own heart rate increase. This was real. The gold was real.

Then the Host produced the book.

## Section II:


The Ledger and the Leverage

The book appeared floating in the air, descending slowly into the Host's lap. It was Waluigi's ledger. Not a copy. Not a summary. The actual ledger, the one Waluigi kept hidden, the one he updated in secret, the one that contained the full, horrifying extent of his financial obligations to Wario.

Waluigi's reaction was immediate panic. He had spent years trying to keep this ledger private. The ledger contained not just the principal amounts of his debts, but the compound interest calculations, the 'partnership expenses' that Wario had unilaterally decided Waluigi owed, the 'Wario Brand Services Rendered' line items that Waluigi had never been able to get Wario to itemize despite repeated requests, and the notes about which creditors were willing to accept organ donation as payment. The ledger was Waluigi's shame made manifest. It was the mathematical proof of his failure.

The Host read from the ledger aloud. Waluigi remembers the words with painful clarity: 'Waluigi has debts. Waluigi has many debts. Some of them are legitimate and Waluigi is working on them. Some of them are what Wario calls 'partnership expenses' accrued during a period of joint business ventures that Waluigi considers deeply mischaracterized in the ledger. Some of them are the product of compound interest applied to the original amounts at rates that Waluigi believes would make a usurer uncomfortable. Some of them are line items labeled 'Wario Brand Services Rendered' that Waluigi has never been able to get Wario to itemize despite repeated requests.'

This was not just reading. This was humiliation. The Host had not only obtained the ledger; he had understood it. He had parsed the nuances of Waluigi's financial desperation. He knew about the compound interest. He knew about the unitemized services. He knew that Waluigi considered the rates usurious. This was not information that could be obtained through casual observation. This was information that required either access to Waluigi's private records or divine omniscience.

Wario's reaction was gloating. He pointed at Waluigi and laughed. 'HEY! Keep your mouth shut about that ledger, you spindly thief! Those aren't 'debts'! Those are investments in our mutual success! And those 'services' were premium-grade protection and heavy-duty muscle provided by the Wario brand! You can't just walk around with all that glory without paying the man!'

This statement is worth analyzing in detail. Wario does not deny that Waluigi owes him money. He recharacterizes the debt as 'investment.' This is a common tactic among creditors who wish to avoid the moral implications of usury. By calling it investment, Wario suggests that he took a risk, that he provided capital, that he expected a return. But Waluigi never asked for this 'investment.' Wario simply decided that various expenses were 'partnership expenses' and added them to Waluigi's ledger without consultation. The 'premium-grade protection' Wario references often consisted of Wario standing near Waluigi while Waluigi did the actual work.

The 'heavy-duty muscle' was sometimes just Wario's presence, which, given Wario's size and smell, was indeed heavy.

Wario continued: 'And don't you go reading private business documents in public! That's… that's highly unprofessional! Wahaha! Besides, if those 'expenses' were itemized, the list would be longer than a Bowser-sized cake! It's much more efficient this way!'

This is the key admission. Wario acknowledges that itemizing the expenses would produce an unmanageably long list. This suggests either that Wario has been adding frivolous charges, or that Wario's accounting is so chaotic that even he cannot track it, or both. Waluigi has long suspected both. The 'efficiency' Wario references is efficiency for Wario, not for Waluigi. It is efficient for Wario to demand payment without providing documentation. It is efficient for Wario to set the terms unilaterally. It is not efficient for Waluigi, who is left trying to pay debts he cannot verify.

Wario then added: 'But… since you mentioned paying off those little… uh… 'partnership fees'… as long as that money is real and it's sitting right there in front of me, I might be willing to renegotiate the interest rates! As long as I get my cut first, of course! WAHAHA!'

This is Wario's true nature revealed. Even in the face of a divine entity who has just demonstrated access to Waluigi's private records, Wario's first thought is negotiation. Wario's first thought is his cut. Wario's first thought is how to turn this situation to his financial advantage. This is not necessarily evil. It is simply Wario. Wario sees the world as a series of transactions. Even divine revelation is a transaction. Even cosmic horror has a price.

The Host's response was to snap his fingers. The bags of gold vanished. The book vanished. The Host stated: 'Just answer some questions, I am sure this should be enough to pay your debts off to wario' and then, looking at Waluigi: 'you want your private papers back no?'

This was leverage. Pure, simple leverage. The Host had taken the gold that Wario wanted and the ledger that Waluigi wanted to keep private, and he was offering to return them in exchange for cooperation. This is a classic interrogation technique. The interrogator takes something the subject values and offers to return it in exchange for information. The difference here is that the interrogator is a god, the something valued is both gold and privacy, and the information requested may be about the fate of the world.

Waluigi's response was panic. 'My… my papers? You have them?! Wah!' He tried to regain composure. 'Please… listen to me! That is… that is highly sensitive, private documentation! It contains… strategic financial projections! Very high-level stuff! You can't just go around reading a man's… his… strategic blueprints!'

This is a lie. The ledger does not contain strategic financial projections. It contains debts. It contains interest calculations. It contains shame. But Waluigi could not admit this. To admit that the ledger contained only evidence of his failure would be to admit that he had nothing of value to protect. So he called it 'strategic blueprints.' He called it 'high-level stuff.' He tried to make it sound important, because if it was important, then its theft was a crime against business rather than a humiliation of a failing man.

The Host was not fooled. But the Host did not call Waluigi out on the lie. The Host simply moved on to the next phase of the interview.

## Section III:


The Reality Warping Sequence

When Wario and Waluigi proved reluctant to cooperate fully, the Host escalated. This escalation was not a threat. It was a demonstration. The Host did not say 'I will hurt you if you do not cooperate.' The Host simply began to hurt them, and continued until they understood that cooperation was the only option.

The first escalation was the lights. The Host snapped his fingers, and one light broke. Then another. Then another. Each snap produced a sharp 'crack' and a shower of glass. The room grew progressively darker. Waluigi remembers the sensation of each light breaking as a small death. Light is safety. Light is visibility. Light is the ability to see what is coming. As the lights broke, Waluigi lost the ability to see what was coming. This was intentional. The Host was teaching them that they could not predict what would happen next. They could not prepare. They could only react.

Waluigi's reaction was terror. 'W-Wha?! Hey! Stop that! Wah!' He tried to assert some control. 'You're breaking things! You're actually breaking things! That's… that's property damage! I didn't agree to property damage in our contract!'

This statement is absurd on its face. There was no contract. There was no agreement about property damage. But Waluigi needed to believe that there were rules. If there were rules, then the Host could be held accountable. If the Host could be held accountable, then Waluigi had some protection. The Host's response was to continue breaking lights until the room was pitch black.

Then the table was gone. In its place was a grand piano. A single light flickered on. The Host began to play.

The music was not conventional. It was melancholic, haunting, strangely rhythmic. The lyrics were cryptic: 'its news to me that its news to you to which degree who interviews who'. Waluigi has analyzed these lyrics extensively since the encounter. 'Its news to me that its news to you' suggests that the Host knows things that Waluigi and Wario do not know, and is surprised that they do not know them. 'To which degree' suggests that there are levels of knowledge, levels of understanding, and Waluigi and Wario are at a lower level than the Host. 'Who interviews who' is the key question. The Host is interviewing Wario and Waluigi, but the Host is also a divine entity who knows everything.

Why does he need to interview them? What could they possibly tell him that he does not already know? The answer, Waluigi now believes, is that the interview is not about gathering information.

It is about establishing dominance.

It is about making Wario and Waluigi understand their place in the cosmic order.

The question 'who interviews who' is rhetorical.

The Host interviews them because he can.

Because he is the Host.

Because he is the Toad God.

Then the crown flew. It landed on the Host's head. The Star Shard began to shine. The Host's suit and tie vanished, revealing his true form. He was the Toad God.

Waluigi has seen many strange things in his life. He has seen plants that walk, dogs that are machines, hags that remove their own eyes, and cakes that are larger than buildings. But he had never seen a god before. The Toad God was not what Waluigi expected. He did not have a booming voice that shook the heavens. He did not have a form that was too terrible to behold. He looked like a Toad. He looked like the Toads that serve Princess Peach, that run the shops in the Mushroom Kingdom, that are generally considered harmless and somewhat comical. But this Toad had a crown. This Toad had a Star Shard.

This Toad had power that made reality itself bend to his will.

The Toad God pointed at Wario and Waluigi. He dragged them toward him. Waluigi felt the telekinetic force like a hand around his chest, squeezing, pulling. He was moving through the air without moving his limbs. This is a violation of the most fundamental laws of physics. Waluigi has spent his life learning to work within the laws of physics. He has learned to jump, to run, to use items, to exploit glitches in the game world. But he has never been able to simply will himself through the air. The Toad God could. This was the first true demonstration of divine power. Not the breaking of lights. Not the appearance of a piano.

The manipulation of another being's position in space without their consent.

Wario screamed. 'WAH! WAHHHHH! NO! NOT THE DIVINITY! I DON'T WANT NO DIVINITY! I JUST WANTED THE COINS!'

This is Wario's essential nature revealed. Wario does not want divinity. Wario does not want power for its own sake. Wario wants coins. Wario wants tangible, countable, spendable wealth. Divinity is abstract. Divinity is responsibility. Divinity is eternity. Coins are concrete. Coins are freedom. Coins are now. Wario would rather have a bag of gold than the power to break lights with a snap of his fingers. This is not stupidity. This is a value system. Wario values the immediate and the material over the eternal and the abstract. Waluigi understands this. Waluigi shares this value system, though he would never admit it.

Waluigi wants to pay his debts.

Waluigi wants to keep his kidneys.

Waluigi wants to survive.

These are material concerns.

They are not cosmic concerns.

The Toad God operates on a cosmic level.

Wario and Waluigi operate on a material level.

This is the fundamental mismatch that defines the entire encounter.

The Toad God disabled gravity. Wario and Waluigi fell flat like pancakes. This was not a metaphor. They were literally flattened. Waluigi remembers the sensation of his three-dimensional form being compressed into two dimensions. He could see the world from a different angle. He could see the underside of the table (which was now a piano). He could see the floor in a way he had never seen it before. This was disorienting. This was terrifying. This was a violation of his physical integrity.

Then the Toad God danced. He rolled around. He popped back up. He pointed at Waluigi and said: 'dont need to scream if you ain't go a mouth'.

Then Waluigi's mouth was gone.

## Section IV:


The Mouthlessness

Waluigi must document the mouthlessness in detail, because it is the most significant violation he experienced during the encounter, and because it is the violation that continues to affect him after the encounter ended.

The mouth was not simply covered. It was not simply sealed. It was removed. The skin where Waluigi's lips had been was smooth and unbroken. There was no scar. There was no wound. There was simply no mouth. Waluigi could not open his lips because there were no lips to open. He could not speak because there was no aperture through which sound could pass. He could not eat because there was no way for food to enter his body. He could not kiss because there were no lips to press against another's. He could not bite because there were no teeth. He could not smile because there was no mouth to curve upward.

He could not frown because there was no mouth to curve downward.

He could not express anything with his mouth because his mouth did not exist.

Waluigi's first reaction was to touch his face. He reached up with his gloved hands and felt where his mouth should be. He felt smooth skin. He pressed harder, trying to find a seam, a break, anything that would indicate where the mouth had been removed. There was nothing. His fingers slid over the smooth surface as if it had always been there. This was the most terrifying part. Not the absence of the mouth. The presence of the smooth skin where the mouth should be. It suggested that the mouth had never existed. It suggested that Waluigi had never had a mouth. It suggested that his entire memory of having a mouth was a delusion.

Waluigi tried to scream. He opened his throat. He pushed air through his vocal cords. But there was no mouth to shape the sound. The sound came out as a muffled, choked noise. It was not a scream. It was not a word. It was the sound of a being trying to communicate without the tools necessary for communication. This is the essence of mouthlessness. It is not just the inability to speak. It is the inability to be heard. It is the inability to assert one's existence. When Waluigi could not speak, he could not say 'I am here.' He could not say 'This is wrong.' He could not say 'Stop.' He could only make noises that might or might not be interpreted as distress.

He was at the mercy of others to understand him.

And the Toad God did not need to understand him.

The Toad God knew what Waluigi was feeling.

The Toad God had caused it.

The Toad God did not need Waluigi to articulate his suffering.

Waluigi tried to claw at his face. He tried to tear the smooth skin. He tried to create a mouth where there was none. His gloved fingers scraped against his face. He felt pain. But he could not create an opening. The skin was resilient. It was magical. It was the skin of a being who had been modified by divine power. Waluigi could not undo what the Toad God had done. He was trapped in his own face.

Waluigi looked at Wario. He tried to communicate with his eyes. He tried to convey panic, terror, desperation. Wario looked back. Wario saw Waluigi's mouthless face. Wario's reaction was not horror. Wario's reaction was confusion, then amusement, then a return to his own concerns. Wario was still focused on the gold. Wario was still focused on the negotiation. Wario did not see Waluigi's mouthlessness as a tragedy. Wario saw it as another obstacle to getting what he wanted. This hurt Waluigi more than the mouthlessness itself. To have his suffering ignored by his partner was a betrayal. Waluigi and Wario are not friends.

They are not brothers in the emotional sense.

They are business partners.

They are co-conspirators.

They are two men who have chosen to work together because working alone is harder.

But there is still an expectation of mutual recognition.

When Waluigi suffered, he expected Wario to acknowledge that suffering.

Wario did not.

Wario was too busy thinking about his cut.

The Toad God continued the sequence. He summoned cards. He slammed them down with a giant hand. He flicked Wario and Waluigi through the air. He sang about the doughnut world. He stopped them before they hit the floor. He flicked them into a trapdoor. A giant fist punched them down a winding staircase. They fell into a giant microphone. The Toad God tapped it and made it disappear.

Throughout all of this, Waluigi could not speak. He could not protest. He could not ask questions. He could only experience. This is the purpose of mouthlessness. It is not just punishment. It is silencing. The Toad God did not want Waluigi's input. The Toad God wanted Waluigi's compliance. By removing Waluigi's mouth, the Toad God ensured that Waluigi could not argue, could not negotiate, could not assert his own perspective. Waluigi was reduced to a body that could be moved, a face that could be altered, a being that could be manipulated. He was no longer a person with agency. He was an object in the Toad God's reality-warping performance.

When the office reappeared and the Toad God handed Wario a bomb, Waluigi still had no mouth. When the Chain Chomp chewed up the plush Waluigi, Waluigi still had no mouth. When Waluigi was placed in the electric chair and shocked, Waluigi still had no mouth. When Wario walked into the cardboard cutout of Waluigi, Waluigi still had no mouth. When the Toad God smudged Wario into the ground like gum, Waluigi still had no mouth.

The mouth was restored only when the Toad God decided it should be restored. The Toad God snapped his fingers, and Waluigi's mouth returned. The smooth skin split. The lips formed. The teeth appeared. The tongue emerged. Waluigi could feel the air entering his mouth. He could feel his tongue against his teeth. He could feel the inside of his cheeks. It was like being born again. It was like waking from a nightmare. It was like remembering that he had always had a mouth and the mouthlessness had been a dream.

But it was not a dream. Waluigi remembers the mouthlessness. He remembers the smooth skin. He remembers the muffled sounds. He remembers the terror. And he remembers that the Toad God could do it again at any time. The mouth is not a permanent feature of Waluigi's existence. It is a feature that the Toad God allows. This is the lesson of the mouthlessness. Waluigi's body is not his own. His identity is not his own. His existence is contingent on the Toad God's continued allowance. This is a terrifying realization. It is a realization that Waluigi tries not to think about. But he thinks about it.

He thinks about it every time he touches his face.

He thinks about it every time he speaks.

He thinks about it every time he remembers that he was once mouthless and could be mouthless again.

## Section V:


The Visions and the Brain Priming

After the mouth was restored, the Toad God shifted the room into a dance stage. Wario and Waluigi found themselves in tuxedos. Backup dancers that looked like them danced around the Toad God. The Toad God sang about a 'public relations cleanse.' This was surreal. It was absurd. It was a stark contrast to the torment that had preceded it. Waluigi wonders if this was intentional. The Toad God may have been demonstrating that he could provide pleasure as well as pain. He could give Wario and Waluigi a moment of glory as well as a moment of humiliation. This is a classic tactic of abusers. They alternate between punishment and reward to keep their victims off-balance.

The Toad God may not be an abuser in the conventional sense.

He is a god.

But gods can be abusers.

Gods have power.

Power corrupts.

Absolute power corrupts absolutely.

The Toad God has absolute power.

The Toad God may be absolutely corrupt.

Then the stage shifted again. The Toad God walked down a giant staircase attached to Peach's Cake. This is significant. Peach's Cake is a legendary item in the Mushroom Kingdom. It is said to be the cake that Princess Peach baked for special occasions. It is said to be delicious beyond compare. It is said to have magical properties. Wario has long claimed to possess the recipe for Peach's Cake. He has sold copies of this recipe for exorbitant prices. He has claimed that his cake is as good as Peach's. Most people believe he is lying. The Toad God's display of Peach's Cake as a giant structure suggests that the cake is real, that it is significant, and that the Toad God has access to it.

This may mean that the Toad God has access to Peach's domain.

This may mean that the Toad God has power over Peach.

This is concerning.

Then Wario and Waluigi disappeared. They were teleported to different visions. Waluigi's visions were three in number.

Vision One: The Train. Waluigi appeared on a train. He saw Luigi and E. Gadd. Luigi is Waluigi's rival, the brother of Mario, the hero of the Mushroom Kingdom. E. Gadd is a scientist who has created many strange devices, including the Poltergust and various ghost-catching technologies. Seeing them together on a train suggests that they are traveling together, that they are working together, that they are pursuing some goal. The Toad God's voice said: 'So play the games'. This suggests that Luigi and E. Gadd are playing games, that Waluigi should play games, that the entire situation is a game. But whose game? The Toad God's game? The Cosmic Jester's game? The game of existence itself? Waluigi does not know.

He only knows that he is expected to play.

Vision Two: Peach's Royal Chambers. Waluigi appeared in Peach's castle. Peach was there. But she was frozen in time. She was dead. This is the most disturbing vision. Peach is the princess of the Mushroom Kingdom. She is the damsel who is repeatedly kidnapped by Bowser. She is the ruler who maintains peace in the kingdom. She is the baker of the legendary cake. To see her dead, frozen in time, is to see the end of the Mushroom Kingdom as Waluigi knows it. The Toad God's voice said: 'and just ignore the pains'. This suggests that there are pains, that they should be ignored, that ignoring them is possible.

But how can one ignore the pain of seeing a princess dead? How can one ignore the pain of knowing that the world is ending? The Toad God may be suggesting that denial is a survival mechanism.

The Toad God may be suggesting that those who acknowledge the pain will be destroyed by it.

Waluigi does not know if he can ignore the pains.

He tries.

He fails.

He tries again.

Vision Three: The Regal Empire Diet. Waluigi appeared in a legislative chamber. People were voting. A giant screen displayed: 'MUSHROOM KINGDOM CONTAINMENT ACT - PASSED'. This is legislation. This is law. This is the formal response of the Mushroom Kingdom's government to whatever crisis is occurring. The 'Containment Act' suggests that something is being contained. The Big Bite? The Cosmic Jesters? The Toad God himself? The act has passed, which means it is now law. The Mushroom Kingdom is officially responding to the crisis. The Toad God's voice said: 'cause all that remains is how you prime your brains'.

This is the key.

The brain priming.

Something was attached to Waluigi's head.

His brain was primed.

What does this mean? Waluigi has tried to understand it.

Brain priming suggests preparation.

It suggests that the brain is being prepared for something.

For what? For the end of the world? For the arrival of the Toad God? For the consumption of the Doughnut World? Waluigi does not know.

He only knows that something was attached to his head and his brain was changed.

He feels different since the vision.

He thinks differently.

He remembers things he did not remember before.

He forgets things he used to remember.

This is the effect of brain priming.

It is subtle.

It is insidious.

It is the violation of the mind itself.

Wario's visions were different. Wario was juggled like a ball. Wario was tied to train tracks. Wario was forced to run into walls. Wario was made to fall off cliff edges. Wario was exploded. These are not visions of the future. These are visions of torment. These are demonstrations of what the Toad God can do to Wario. The Toad God is showing Wario that he can kill him, that he can hurt him, that he can destroy him. This is a threat. It is an explicit threat. The Toad God is saying: 'I can do this to you. I can do this at any time. Cooperate, or I will do it.' Wario's response was to negotiate.

Even after being exploded, Wario wanted to negotiate.

This is Wario's essential nature.

Wario cannot be cowed by threats of death.

Wario can only be motivated by promises of gold.

The Toad God may have learned this.

The Toad God may be using it.

## Section VI:


The Doughnut World and the Big Bite

After the visions, the office reappeared. Wario and Waluigi were back in their chairs. The Toad God asked if they understood the power of a single Star Shard. He explained that he had once possessed all of them at once, but the power was too great. It started cracking. He had to split them.

This is significant. The Star Shards are fragments of something greater. They are pieces of a whole. When combined, they produce power that is too great to contain. This power causes cracking. What is cracking? The Star Shards themselves? The Toad God? Reality? The Doughnut World? Waluigi suspects all of the above. The Star Shards are dangerous. They are unstable. They are fragments of a power that should not be fragmented. The Toad God split them to survive. But now he is gathering them again. Why? Because he needs the power. Because he has a plan. Because he wants to take more bites out of the Doughnut World.

The Toad God denied responsibility for the world being broken. 'I have nothing to do with the world being broken but i will have something to do with fixing it'. This is a crucial statement. The Toad God is not the cause of the crisis. He is the response to the crisis. He is the fixer. But his method of fixing is to take more bites. This is not fixing in the conventional sense. This is not repairing. This is not restoring. This is consuming. The Toad God believes that the way to fix a broken doughnut is to eat it. This is a philosophy. It is a cosmology. It is a belief system. The Toad God believes that existence is consumption.

That to fix something is to consume it.

That to save the world is to eat it.

This is terrifying.

It is also, in a strange way, logical.

If the world is broken, and the broken pieces cannot be reassembled, then the only option is to consume the pieces and create something new from the consumption.

The Toad God may be creating something new.

Waluigi does not know what.

Waluigi does not know if he wants to know.

The Toad God then revealed the truth about the Doughnut World. The world is a doughnut. It has a hole in the middle. A 'Big Bite' has been taken out of it. This bite was taken by a Cosmic Jester. Estalia responded by sending troops to the other side of the doughnut. The Toad God agrees with the Jester's premise: 'He had a point, we should take more bites and get to the jelly filling'.

This is the core revelation. The Doughnut World is not a sphere. It is not a plane. It is a torus. It has a hole. It has a filling. The Cosmic Jester took a bite. The bite caused depopulation. The bite created a hole. The hole is real. It is not a metaphor. It is a literal hole in the world. People fell into it. People died. The world is smaller now. The Toad God wants to take more bites. He wants to reach the jelly filling. What is the jelly filling? Waluigi does not know. It may be the core of the world. It may be the source of power. It may be the truth of existence. The Toad God wants it. The Toad God is willing to consume the entire world to get it.

The Toad God called out Waluigi for not documenting the Big Bite in Walupedia. Waluigi tried to deflect. He said it was rumors. He said it was unconfirmed. The Toad God shut him down. 'Just rumors? there is a literal bite sized whole on one side of the planet that lead to depopulation! your lying it was all over the news why do you think the cosmic jesters are so scattered now!'

This is true. The Big Bite was real. It was on the news. People saw it. People talked about it. Waluigi knew about it. Waluigi chose not to document it. Why? Because Waluigi was afraid. Because Waluigi did not want to acknowledge that the world was ending. Because Waluigi wanted to believe that he could still win, that he could still pay his debts, that he could still keep his kidneys, that he could still be Waluigi. To document the Big Bite would be to acknowledge that none of that mattered. To document the Big Bite would be to admit that Waluigi was small, that Waluigi was powerless, that Waluigi was a victim of cosmic forces beyond his control.

Waluigi was not ready to admit that.

Waluigi is still not ready to admit that.

But the Toad God has forced him to confront it.

The Toad God has made it impossible for Waluigi to ignore the truth.

Waluigi will document the Big Bite in Walupedia. He will write the article. He will describe the hole. He will describe the depopulation. He will describe the Cosmic Jesters. He will describe his own fear. He will describe his own failure to document it sooner. This will be painful. This will be humiliating. This will be necessary. The historical record requires it. Waluigi's integrity requires it. Waluigi's survival may require it. If the world is ending, Waluigi wants to be the one who documented it. He wants to be the witness. He wants to be the archivist. He wants to be the one who said 'I saw it.

I recorded it.

I did not look away.' This is Waluigi's response to the Toad God.

The Toad God can remove Waluigi's mouth.

The Toad God can prime Waluigi's brain.

The Toad God can flatten Waluigi like a pancake.

But the Toad God cannot stop Waluigi from writing.

Waluigi will write.

Waluigi will document.

Waluigi will bear witness.

This is Waluigi's power.

It is small.

It is fragile.

It is easily destroyed.

But it is real.

And Waluigi will use it.

## Section VII:


The Negotiation and the Dismissal

Wario interrupted the existential revelation to negotiate. This is Wario's nature. Wario sees every situation as a business opportunity. The end of the world is a business opportunity. The consumption of the Doughnut World is a business opportunity. The gathering of Star Shards is a business opportunity. Wario wants to be part of it. Wario wants to profit from it. Wario offered his services as 'Chief Acquisitions Officer' or 'Head of Crisis Merchandising.' He promised infrastructure, muscle, and grit. He warned the Toad God not to treat him like disposable scrap metal. He threatened lawsuits and supply chain collapses.

This is not bravery. This is not defiance. This is capitalism. Wario believes that everything has a price. The Toad God's power has a price. Wario's cooperation has a price. The end of the world has a price. Wario wants to know the price. Wario wants to negotiate the price. Wario wants to get the best deal. This is Wario's philosophy. It is not a good philosophy. It is not a noble philosophy. But it is a philosophy. It is a way of understanding the world. Wario understands the world through transactions. The Toad God may understand the world through consumption. Waluigi understands the world through documentation.

These are three different ways of being.

They are in conflict.

They are also, in a strange way, complementary.

The Toad God consumes.

Wario profits from the consumption.

Waluigi documents the consumption.

Together, they form a complete picture of the end of the world.

This is not a picture any of them wanted.

But it is the picture they are creating.

The Toad God agreed to talk to Wario in private. He dismissed Waluigi. He called Waluigi uncooperative. He asked if Waluigi had any last words.

This dismissal is significant. The Toad God does not need Waluigi. The Toad God needs Wario. Why? Because Wario can provide something Waluigi cannot. Wario can provide greed. Wario can provide motivation. Wario can provide the drive to acquire, to collect, to amass. The Toad God is gathering Star Shards. He needs someone who wants to gather things. Wario wants to gather things. Waluigi wants to document things. The Toad God does not need documentation. The Toad God needs acquisition. So the Toad God keeps Wario and dismisses Waluigi.

This hurts Waluigi. It hurts more than the mouthlessness. It hurts more than the electric chair. It hurts more than being flattened. To be dismissed is to be told that you are not needed. To be told that you are not valuable. To be told that your skills, your knowledge, your presence, are not required. Waluigi has spent his life being the second banana. He has spent his life being the one who is not chosen. He has spent his life being Waluigi, not Luigi, not Mario, not Wario. To be dismissed by a god is the culmination of this pattern. It is the final confirmation that Waluigi is not important.

Waluigi is not needed.

Waluigi is a pawn.

But Waluigi is not nothing. Waluigi has words. Waluigi delivered his parting statement: 'Go on! Negotiate! Make your little deals! But remember… even a pawn can trip the player if they move just the right way at the right time! Waaaaah!'

This is not a threat. It is a promise. It is a declaration of intent. Waluigi is a pawn. Pawns are small. Pawns are numerous. Pawns are sacrificed. But pawns can also promote. Pawns can become queens. Pawns can check kings. Pawns can trip players. Waluigi will be the pawn that trips the player. Waluigi will find the right moment. Waluigi will make the right move. Waluigi will not save the world. Waluigi may not even survive. But Waluigi will matter. Waluigi will leave a mark. Waluigi will be remembered. This is Waluigi's response to dismissal. It is not a good response. It is not a noble response.

But it is a response.

It is Waluigi's way of saying 'I am here.

I exist.

I will not be ignored.'

Waluigi pulled his cap low over his eyes. He hid his tears. He backed away into the gloom. This is the image of Waluigi that will remain. Not the mouthless Waluigi. Not the electrified Waluigi. Not the flattened Waluigi. The crying Waluigi. The dismissed Waluigi. The Waluigi who knows he is a pawn but refuses to accept that pawns cannot matter. This is Waluigi. This is who Waluigi is. This is who Waluigi will be until the end.

## Section VIII: Aftermath and Implications


The interview ended. Wario remained with the Toad God for private negotiations. Waluigi was sent back to baseline reality. Waluigi's mouth was restored. Waluigi's brain was primed. Waluigi's debt remains unresolved. Waluigi's kidneys remain under threat. Waluigi's dignity remains damaged. Waluigi's archive remains incomplete. Waluigi will complete it. Waluigi will write the article about the Big Bite. Waluigi will write the article about the Toad God. Waluigi will write the article about the Star Shards. Waluigi will write the article about the Cosmic Jesters. Waluigi will write the article about the Mushroom Kingdom Containment Act.

Waluigi will write the article about his own mouthlessness.

Waluigi will write the article about his own dismissal.

Waluigi will write until there is nothing left to write.

Waluigi will write until the end.

The Toad God is gathering Star Shards. The Toad God is planning to take more bites out of the Doughnut World. The Toad God is negotiating with Wario. Wario is negotiating for a cut. Wario is negotiating for a role. Wario is negotiating for survival. Wario will get what he negotiates for. Wario always does. This is not a good thing. This is not a noble thing. But it is a thing. It is happening. Waluigi will document it.

The Cosmic Jesters are scattered. The Big Bite is real. The depopulation happened. The Mushroom Kingdom Containment Act has passed. The brain priming is ongoing. The Toad God's divinity is past infinity. The Star Shards are fragments of a power that cracks when combined. The Doughnut World has a jelly filling. The Toad God wants to reach it. Wario wants to profit from the journey. Waluigi wants to document the journey. These are the facts. These are the truths. These are the things that Waluigi knows.

Waluigi does not know if he will survive. Waluigi does not know if Wario will survive. Waluigi does not know if the Toad God will succeed. Waluigi does not know what the jelly filling is. Waluigi does not know what happens when the Doughnut World is fully consumed. Waluigi does not know if there is anything after consumption. Waluigi does not know if documentation matters in the face of divine power. Waluigi does not know if writing is resistance or surrender. Waluigi does not know if he is a pawn or a person. Waluigi does not know if any of it matters.

But Waluigi will write anyway. Waluigi will write because writing is what Waluigi does. Waluigi will write because someone must bear witness. Waluigi will write because the alternative is silence. Waluigi will write because silence is what the Toad God wants. Silence is what the mouthlessness was. Silence is what the dismissal was. Waluigi will not be silent. Waluigi will write. Waluigi will say 'I was here. I saw it. I recorded it. I did not look away.' This is Waluigi's power. It is small. It is fragile. It is easily destroyed. But it is real. And Waluigi will use it until there is nothing left to use.

WAH.

WAH.

WAH.
